turns.doctor_question: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. ____. Yeah, um... I came in because I just feel like I’m literally crawling out of my skin whenever I’m supposed to sit still. Like, especially in the radiology suite at work or in my college classes. Actually, the radiology suite is always freezing, which you'd think would keep you alert, but they have to keep it cold for the imaging machines. The MRI magnets are insane, by the way—my buddy Dave accidentally brought a metal clipboard too close once and it practically flew out of his hands. We thought the lead tech was gonna murder him, it was a whole huge ordeal. 

But, uh, anyway, where was I? Right, sitting still. I've been trying to just tough it out for months now, but I just can't do it. I always end up pacing around the control room, or shifting in my chair constantly, or just finding some random excuse to get up and move around. Dave says I'm like a wind-up toy, which is rich coming from a guy who drinks like four energy drinks a shift, you know? But yeah, I just can't stop moving.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient gets distracted by unrelated thoughts about the cold room and a coworker's mistake, losing their train of thought.
symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient reports constantly shifting in their chair.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient mentions finding random excuses to get up and move around when expected to sit still in class or at work.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes feeling like they are 'crawling out of my skin' when supposed to sit still and ends up pacing.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient states they 'just can't stop moving' and are described by a friend as being 'like a wind-up toy'.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been using any stimulants, like caffeine pills, cocaine, amphetamines, or energy drinks, before these episodes?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't really touch any of that. Like I said, Dave's the one pounding energy drinks. He gets those massive white cans, the zero-sugar ones? I tried a sip once because the vending machine on the third floor was completely out of Sprite. Actually, that vending machine is the absolute worst. It ate my dollar last week when I was trying to get a bag of pretzels before my anatomy lab. Anatomy is brutal this semester, by the way. We had to memorize all the bones in the wrist and there's this stupid acronym for it, but I always mix up the trapezoid and trapezium. It's like, why name them basically the exact same thing? Whoever named bones was definitely not thinking about college students. But, uh... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, drugs and caffeine. Yeah, no, I don't use any of that. Not even coffee.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates being easily distracted by unrelated thoughts, drifting from energy drinks to vending machines and anatomy class before forgetting the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient talks excessively, providing a long, rambling, and tangential response to a straightforward yes/no question.

turns.doctor_question: Were you like this as a child, too?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, oh man, absolutely. My parents actually still talk about my elementary school parent-teacher conferences. Apparently, every single year the teachers would say the exact same thing—that I was constantly out of my seat, calling out answers, or rushing ahead before they even finished giving directions. It was a whole thing way before middle school, definitely not just something that started since my radiology training. 

Speaking of elementary school, did you ever have to do those parachute games in P.E.? Where everyone grabs a handle and you lift it up and run underneath? That was literally the best part of being a kid. We had this one gym teacher, Mr. Henderson, who always wore these super short shorts, like, neon 80s style. He was a character. He actually caught me climbing the rope in the gym once when we weren't supposed to, and I got sent to the principal's office. The principal's office smelled exactly like the waiting room at my dentist's office, which is weird, right? Like, old magazines and mint. I hate the dentist. But yeah, to answer your question, I've pretty much always been like this.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates distractibility by unrelated thoughts, going on a tangent about parachute games, their gym teacher, and the smell of the dentist's office.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient explicitly states that teachers reported they were 'constantly out of my seat' in elementary school.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient recalls a specific instance of inappropriate climbing, stating they were 'caught climbing the rope in the gym once when we weren't supposed to.'
symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient mentions a history of 'calling out answers' and 'rushing ahead before they even finished giving directions.'

turns.doctor_question: Do you often have trouble paying close attention to details or make careless mistakes when you’re doing schoolwork or tasks at work?
turns.patient_response:
Careless mistakes? Um... not really, no. I mean, I don't think so. I actually try to be pretty careful, especially at work, because, you know, radiation. You really don't want to mess around with that. We have to wear those heavy lead aprons whenever we're doing portable X-rays, and they weigh a ton. I actually threw my back out a little bit last month lifting one off the rack wrong. My mom told me to go see a chiropractor, but I don't really trust them. I saw this video on YouTube where a guy got his neck cracked and it sounded like a dry branch snapping in half. Ugh, makes me shudder just thinking about it. 

YouTube is wild, though. I started watching this one channel where this guy restores old rusty tools, like axes and wrenches and stuff. It's super satisfying to watch all the rust come off in the chemical bath. I actually wanted to try it myself, so I bought this antique hammer at a flea market, but it's just been sitting in my trunk for like three weeks. My trunk is a disaster right now, honestly. I have like four empty windshield washer fluid jugs back there. 

But, uh, wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, details and mistakes. Yeah, no, I'm usually pretty good about the details. I haven't really noticed any problems with that.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient explicitly denies making careless mistakes or having trouble with details, stating they are 'usually pretty good about the details.'
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient becomes easily distracted by their own unrelated thoughts (work, chiropractors, YouTube, their car trunk) and loses track of the doctor's original question.
symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient talks excessively, providing a long, rambling, and tangential response to a simple yes/no question.

turns.doctor_question: Do you spend a lot of time worrying about different things, even when there’s nothing specific happening?
turns.patient_response:
Worrying? Um, not really. I mean, I don't just sit around stressing about random stuff when nothing's going on. My mom does that enough for the both of us, honestly. She's always texting me to make sure I locked my apartment door or asking if I'm eating enough vegetables. Which, I mean, I'm probably not, but who actually eats enough vegetables in college? I tried making a salad last week, but I bought that pre-washed spinach in the plastic tub and it went slimy in the fridge after like two days. Why does it go bad so fast? It's a total scam. 

It's kind of like how printer ink costs more than human blood per ounce. I read that on Reddit once. Reddit is super distracting, honestly. I can scroll on there for hours looking at stupid memes or people arguing about movies. I got into this massive debate the other day about whether the new Batman movie is better than The Dark Knight. It's obviously not. Heath Ledger was a genius. Did you know he actually improvised that part where the hospital explodes and the detonator stops working? It's crazy how actors just come up with that stuff on the spot. 

Wait, hospital... right. Sorry, what was the question again? Oh, right, worrying. Uh, yeah, no. I don't really worry about things unless there's an actual reason to. I'm usually pretty chill about that kind of stuff.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates distractibility by getting sidetracked by unrelated thoughts (spinach, printer ink, Reddit, Batman) and forgetting the doctor's question.
symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient talks excessively, providing a long, rambling response filled with unrelated tangents before returning to the question.
symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies spending time worrying about random things when nothing specific is happening.

turns.doctor_question: Did you also have trouble staying focused or finishing things as a child?
turns.patient_response:
Focused? Um, no, not really. I don't remember having a hard time finishing things when I was a kid. I mean, I was always bouncing off the walls, sure, but if I was doing something, I usually got it done. Especially if it was something I liked, like building stuff. I had this massive collection of Legos. I mean, tubs and tubs of them. I'd dump them all out on the living room floor and build these giant spaceships. 

My dad stepped on a Lego once in the middle of the night and I swear he learned some new curse words that day. It's crazy how much those little plastic bricks hurt, right? It's like stepping on a landmine. I actually saw a documentary once about how they manufacture Legos, and the precision they use is insane. Like, the molds have to be perfect down to the micrometer or they won't snap together right. It's kind of like the calibration we do on the X-ray machines at school. If the alignment is off even a tiny bit, the image is totally useless. We had a lab practical last week and this one girl forgot to set the SID right and completely missed the joint she was trying to shoot. The instructor was so mad. 

Instructors in college are way more intense than high school teachers. My high school biology teacher used to just let us watch Planet Earth half the time. David Attenborough's voice is so soothing. I could listen to him read a phone book. Do they even make phone books anymore? I feel like I haven't seen one in like ten years. 

But anyway, yeah, um, finishing things as a kid? No, I don't think I had a problem with that. Just the sitting still part.

symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient describes their childhood behavior as 'always bouncing off the walls.'
symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient provides a very lengthy, rambling response to a simple yes/no question.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech demonstrates marked tangentiality, drifting from Legos to X-ray machines to David Attenborough before finally returning to the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly denies having trouble staying focused as a child ('Focused? Um, no, not really.').
symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient denies having a hard time finishing things, stating they usually got tasks done.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself worrying almost every day about a lot of different things?
turns.patient_response:
Every day? No, I wouldn't say that. Like I said, I'm pretty laid back unless there's an actual reason to stress out. My roommate, though, he's a totally different story. He worries about literally everything. He's a nursing major, and he's always convinced he's failing his clinicals even when he gets A's. He drinks so much coffee it's a miracle his heart hasn't exploded. We have this espresso machine in our apartment that we got off Facebook Marketplace for like fifty bucks. It's one of those fancy Italian ones, but the steam wand is totally broken. 

I tried to fix it last weekend. I took the whole casing off and everything, but the boiler was totally calcified. Hard water is the worst. It ruins everything. It leaves those gross white spots on the shower doors, too. I bought this special cleaner for it, but it smells like straight vinegar. I hate the smell of vinegar. It reminds me of dyeing Easter eggs when I was a kid. We used to use those little PAAS kits with the wire dipper thing. I always ended up mixing all the colors together until the eggs just looked like muddy brown rocks. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, worrying every day. Yeah, no, I don't really do that. I just kind of take things as they come.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient gets easily distracted by a chain of unrelated thoughts (roommate, espresso machine, hard water, Easter eggs) and loses track of the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient provides a long, rambling monologue that goes far off-topic, demonstrating excessive talking.
symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies worrying every day, stating he is laid back and takes things as they come.
